output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% looks like ordinary week-to-week variation, not a fault from v4.18. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. This week's 0.411% sits inside that band. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). Three earlier weeks went higher, and investigating them found nothing. The dashboard count matches raw logs, so it isn't a counting artefact. Booking completion didn't change, and support got no complaints. The "new pods error at twice the rate" finding is a warm-up effect. Every recent rollout, including a config-only redeploy with no code change, shows the same gap, because new pods start with empty caches and time out against the database. That adds only 10–20 errors per rollout. I could not rule out the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic as small contributors, but nothing needs acting on. Recommendation: don't roll back, don't move the replica back, and don't mute alerting. Muting would remove the protection that matters. Record the week at ops review and run the standard check on the following week. If next week exceeds the band, open an incident. Confidence is fairly high, but the cause of the small bump is unknown.
